fields.why: Every quantity (trial seroresponse table, safety, VFC and MarketScan completion) is cited to the package insert or ACIP presentations (refs 3, 4) to frame a recommendation, which fits 'limited'. 'yes' is defensible because the report tabulates comparative estimates with 95% CIs, some from unpublished data.

Series completion is compared between MenB-4C and MenB-FHbp within VFC-eligible and VFC-ineligible strata, a comparison within levels of a third variable. A quoted this very passage but recorded only comparison.

The main claim (the new schedule improves protection) rests on the Table, which compares three schedule/dose conditions, so group is preferred. Pair is defensible as two schedules, or as the MenB-4C vs MenB-FHbp completion contrast that B cites, though that contrast is secondary.

The report is an ACIP recommendation that summarizes cited trial and claims evidence. It contains no original analysis, so mixed/other adds nothing. A rule is needed: guidance reports that only summarize cited evidence take 'guidance or recommendations' alone, and the list has no trial design to describe the underlying studies.

The VFC note defines eligibility partly by American Indian or Alaska Native status, so race/ethnicity is a defensible descriptor inside the composite VFC stratifier. Omitting it is also defensible, and it does not change level 2.

brief_issues: No rule decides whether an ACIP recommendation report that tabulates cited evidence with CIs counts as 'limited' or 'yes'. No rule says how to treat a composite eligibility stratifier (VFC = insurance status plus AI/AN). Setting is ambiguous when immunogenicity data come from multinational trials (about 30% US) but completion data are US national; both readers chose US national and said so in their notes.
